:JUDGMENT:

This Claim Petition is filed by the Petitioners against the Respondents under Section 166 of the Motor Vehicles Act seeking Compensation of Rs.80,00,000/- for the death of Sri. SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Sachin S.A, S/o Anantharamu in a Road Traffic accident.

2. The substance of averments made in the Petition is as under:
That on 28.11.2022 between 2.30 to 2.35 p.m., when the son of the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by name Sachin was riding his motor cycle bearing Reg No.KA-11-ES-0164 and when he reached at Chattamgere Circle, near Chattamgere Village, Shilanere Hobli,
Krishnarajpet Taluk, Mandya District, at that time, the rider of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-L-7301 came in a rash and negligent manner and dashed against the Sachin's motor cycle.

Due to the said impact, Sachin fell down and sustained grievous injuries and he was succumbed to the injuries in JSS hospital and thereafter Post Mortem was conducted and dead body was handed over to the Petitioners.
Prior to the date of accident, the deceased was hale and healthy and he was working as a Supervisor in Tirumala Enterprises and was earning Rs.40,000/- per month.
The Petitioners entirely depending upon the income of the deceased.
SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-L- 7301.

Therefore,
the Respondent No.1 and 2 are jointly and severally liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
3. In pursuance of service of Notice to the Respondents, Respondent No.1 and 2 appeared before the Court through their respective Counsels.
The Respondent No.2 did not choose to file Objection Statement.
The Respondent No.1 has filed its Objection Statement to the main Petition.

sentences.text: The Respondent No.1 in its Objection Statement denied the age, avocation and income of the deceased and the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle and also the death of the deceased Sachin in the said accident.
Further it admits the issuance of the policy.
It further contended that at the time of the accident the rider of the offending motor cycle was not hold valid and effective driving license and thereby violated the policy conditions.
SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Further it contended that the Jurisdictional police have filed Charge sheet for the offences punishable under Sec.3 r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act.
Further it contended that the alleged accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the deceased himself.

Hence,
it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On these grounds, the Respondent No.1 has prayed to dismiss the Petition against it.

4. On the basis of the rival pleadings, this Tribunal has framed the following Issues:
ISSUES 1) Whether the Petitioners prove that Sachin S.A. S/o Anantharamu was died in the Road Traffic Accident that occurred on 28.11.2022 in between 2.30 to 2.35 p.m., near Chattamgere circle, Chattamgere village, Shilanere Hobli, Krishnarajpet Taluk,
Mandya District, due to rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing Reg.No.KA-54-L-7301?
2) Whether the Petitioners further prove that they are the legal heirs of deceased Sachin S.A?
SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 3) Whether the Petitioners are entitled for the compensation as prayed for?

If yes,
what is the quantum and who is liable to pay ?
4) What Order or Award ?
6.

Further, they examined one witness as PW.2 and got marked 2 documents at Ex.P16 & 17 and closed their side evidence.
The Respondent No.1 has examined one witness as RW.1 and got marked one document at Ex.R1 and closed its side evidence.

SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023  REASONS 8. Issue No.1: It is the case of the Petitioners that the son of the Petitioner No.1 and 2 by name Sachin was died in the accident that occurred due to the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the motorcycle bearing No.KA-54-L-7301.
9. On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 has denied the accident occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending vehicle.

10. In order to prove the case of the Petitioners, Petitioner No.3 got examined herself as PW.1 and she has filed her chief affidavit in lieu of chief examination and re-iterated the averments made in the Petition.

sentences.text: Ex.P.7 is the IMV report which shows that the accident does not caused due to any mechanical defects of the vehicles.

12. P.W.1 is subjected for cross-examination by the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1.

But,
nothing could be elicited to disbelieve the version of the PW.1.
PW.1 has also examined Medical Record Officer by name Shivananda Swamy as PW.2 and got marked Case sheet and MLC Register extract at Ex.P16 and 17.
To rebut the evidence of PW.1, the Respondent No.1 has examined its Legal Manager by name Vinay Prasad as RW.1.
RW.1 in the cross-examination he admitted that in the Charge-sheet there was only one accused.
Upon going through the police records it clearly shows that this accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding of the rider of the offending motorcycle.
The Charge-sheet is the material document which is not challenged by the rider of the motorcycle.

Having regard to the facts and circumstances of the SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 case,
this Tribunal is of the opinion that the PW.1 has proved the accident caused by the rash and negligent riding of the motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-L-7301 by its rider and in the said accident her brother Sachin was succumbed to the injuries.

Accordingly, I answer Issue No.1 is in the "Affirmative".
13. Issue No.2 and 3: Both these Issues are taken together for common discussion as they are interlinked with each other and to avoid repetition of facts.
14.
It is averred in the Petition that the Petitioner No.1 is the father of the deceased, Petitioner No.2 is the mother of the deceased and Petitioner No.3 is the elder sister of the deceased Sachin.
To prove their relationship with the deceased, PW.1 has produced Aadhaar cards of the deceased and their Aadhaar cards which marked at Ex.P.11 to Ex.P.14.
Upon going through the same, it clearly shows the relationship of the deceased Sachin with the Petitioners.
Hence, the Petitioners have proved SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 that they are the legal heirs of the deceased Sachin.
In the cross-examination PW.1 admitted that as on the date of the accident, she was working as a Software Engineer and she is receiving salary of Rs.40,000/- p.m. and she is unmarried.
The very evidence of PW.1 shows that she is not dependent on the income of the deceased.
So, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are only the dependents of the deceased Sachin.
15. Further, the Petitioners have stated the age of the deceased Sachin was 23 years at the time of the accident.
In this regard Petitioners have produced Ex.P14 i.e., Aadhaar card of the deceased which shows the date of birth of the deceased was 03.01.2000.
The accident took place on 28.11.2022.
That means, as on the date of accident, the age of the deceased Sachin was 22 years, 10 month and 25 days.
Hence, the age of the deceased Sachin to be taken at 23 years for the purpose of assessment.

But, PW.1 has not produced any document in this regard.
Therefore, in the absence of income proof, the notional income to be taken at Rs.15,500/- per month for the purpose of assessment of compensation.
17. With this background, the quantum of compensation to which the Petitioners are entitled may be adjudicated.

For the sake of convenience, discussion may be had under following heads :
I. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF CONSORTIUM, COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF ESTATE, COMPENSATION TOWARDS FUNERAL EXPENSES:
18.
The deceased has left behind his mother, father and sister.
Hence, the Petitioner No.1 and 2 are considered as dependents.

At this juncture, I would like to go through principles laid down in the decision reported in Special Leave SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others) wherein Hon'ble Apex Court has pleased to observed that: "Loss of estate has to be compensated by awarding Rupees 15,000/-,
loss of consortium should be Rupees 40,000/- and funeral expenses should be Rupees 15,000/-".

entities.text: Special Leave SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Petition (Civil) No.25590/2014 (National Insurance Company Limited V/s Pranay Sethi and Others
entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: It is further observed that the aforesaid Judgment amount should be enhanced at the rate of 10% in every three years.
The said Judgment was rendered on 30.10.2017.

By applying the said observation made in the aforesaid case, since, more than 6 years lapsed from the date of Order, the consortium fixed in the said case should be enhanced from Rs.40,000/- to Rs.48,400/-.
Further, the loss of estate and funeral expenses also extended to Rs.18,150/- each.

19. As this Court has already observed that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are the mother, father and sister of the deceased Sachin, they are entitled for a sum of Rupees 48,400/- each towards loss of consortium and Rupees 18,150/- towards loss SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 of estate and Rupees 18,150/- towards funeral expenses.
IV. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF LOVE AND AFFECTION 20.
The Petitioner No.1 and 2 are the parents and they lost their son's love and care.
Petitioner No.3 is the sister had lost her brother's love and care.
Bearing in mind the relationship of the Petitioners with the deceased, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.50,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.
V. COMPENSATION TOWARDS TRANSPORTATION OF DEAD BODY:
21. The Petitioners might have spent some amount towards transportation of body of the deceased.
Hence, I am of the opinion that awarding compensation of Rs.5,000/- under this head would be just and reasonable.

VII. COMPENSATION TOWARDS LOSS OF DEPENDANCY:

sentences.text: It is pertinent to note here that as per the detailed discussion as made supra, the income of the deceased was notionally fixed at Rs.15,500/- p.m.

At this juncture, I would like to go through the decision reported in :
1) 2018 ACJ 740, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India At New Delhi in between Manuswamy and others V/s.
Managing Director, Tamil Nadu State Trans. Corpn. Ltd, wherein it is held as under:

- Held : - yes.
2) 2018 ACJ 5, the Hon'ble Supreme Court of India, at New Delhi in between Hem Raj Vs. Oriental Insurance Co. Ltd., and others wherein it is held as under :

dead body 6. Loss of Dependency Rs.23,43,600/-
Thus, totally the Petitioners are awarded compensation of SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Rs.25,80,100/- with costs and simple interest at 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition till the date of realization.

25. Regarding Liability:- This Court has arrived at the conclusion that the accident has been occurred by the rash and negligent riding on the part of the rider of the offending motor cycle bearing No.KA-54-L-7301.
The Respondent No.1 is the insurer and the Respondent No.2 is the owner of the offending motorcycle.

sentences.text: It is the specific contention of the Respondent No.1 that, the rider of the offending motorcycle was not holding DL at the time of the accident.
Further it is the argument of the Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 that the alleged accident was occurred after the amendment to the IMV Act.
Therefore, it is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
It is the further contention of the Respondent No.1 that the owner of the offending motorcycle is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On the other hand, it is the contention of the Petitioners that at the time of the accident, the policy of the offending vehicle was valid.
Hence, the Respondent No.1 being the insurer is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
28. In order to prove the contentions of the Respondent No.1, it has examined its officer by name Vinay Prasad as RW.1 and he reiterated the Written Statement contentions in his chief affidavit.

However, Ex.P6 is the Charge sheet which shows that after thorough investigation, the I.O has also Charge-sheeted the rider of the offending motorcycle for the offences punishable under Sec.3 r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act for not holding DL at the time of the accident.

It is pertinent to note here that the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider of the motorcycle, though, he appeared before the Court through his Counsel, he did not choose to file his Objection Statement.
Further he being the owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle ought to produce his DL, but, he has not produced the DL before the SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Court.
Further, the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle had not entered the witness box.

29. In MFA No.6154/2019 (MV-D) in between Hemalatha @ Hema @ Hemavathi and others Vs.
Bajaj Allianz General Insurance Company Ltd., wherein the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to discussed regarding liability, when the driver of the offending vehicle did not possess the driving license and it has pleased to observed in the said Judgment that the Respondent No.2 - the owner of the vehicle neither contested the petition by filing Written Statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that he did not consciously permit the rider of the vehicle to ride the vehicle.
Further, it has pleased to observed that the rider of the vehicle has ridden without driving license was not impeached by him. Hence, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the Respondent No.2 permitted operating of the vehicle by an unauthorized person and the said act of Respondent No.2 amounts to fundamental SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 breach of policy condition within the meaning of Sec.149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act.

sentences.text: Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition.

Accordingly, the Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka has pleased to partly allowed the appeal and confirmed the dismissal of the claim petition against the Respondent No.1.
30.

In the instant case also, the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle appeared before the Court through his Counsel, but, he did not choose to contest the matter by filing the Written Statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that he ridden the vehicle by possessing Driving license.

Further the Charge sheet clearly shows that the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle was Charge sheeted for the offences Ananthramu vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150599696/
9 punishable under Sec.3 r/w Sec.181 of IMV Act along with the other offences.

sentences.text: Therefore, this Tribunal is also of the opinion that the SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 above said Judgment of our Hon'ble High Court of Karnataka is aptly applicable to the case in hand.
31. In this case, the owner - Respondent No.2 has maintained silence which itself sufficient proof of defence taken by the Respondent No.1.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recovery, when there is a clear breach of policy condition and the liability to pay compensation is on the owner of the vehicle.

32. The Learned Counsel for the Respondent No.1 has relied on the Sec.149 of IMV Act (old) and Sec.150 of IMV Act (New) which reads about "Duty of insurers to satisfy Judgments and Awards against persons insured in respect of third party risks."

The Sec.150(2) (a) (ii) of IMV Act speaks that no sum shall be payable by an insurer under sub Sec.(1) in respect of any Judgment or Award unless, before commencement of the proceedings in which the Judgment or Award is given the insurer had notice through the Court or, as the case may be, SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such Judgment or Award so long as its execution is stayed pending in appeal, and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of such any proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party thereto, and to defend the action on any of the grounds, namely:-
(a) That there has been a breach of a specific condition of the policy, being one of the following conditions, namely:-
(ii) a condition excluding driving by a named person or by any person who is not duly licensed or by any person who has been disqualified for holding or obtaining a driving license during the period of disqualification or driving under the influence of alcohol or drugs as laid down in Sec.185.
33.
In this case, the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider neither filed his Objection Statement nor he stepped into the witness box to speak about his driving license.
Further he did not produce his driving license.
The amendment to the SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 IMV Act was came into effect from April 1, 2022 and the alleged accident has been occurred on 28.11.2022 i.e., after amendment to the IMV Act.
Hence, this Tribunal is of the considered opinion that the act of the Respondent No.2 amounts to the fundamental breach of the policy condition.
Therefore, the Respondent No.2 is liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
On the other hand, the Respondent No.1 is not liable to pay compensation to the Petitioners.
Accordingly, I answer Issue No.2 "in the Affirmative" and Issue No.3 "Partly in the Affirmative".
34. Issue No.4:
From the above discussion, I am of the opinion that the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for compensation of Rs.25,80,100/- along with interest at the rate of 6% p.a. from the date of the Petition.

In the result, I proceed to pass the following:
ORDER

The Claim Petition filed by the SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 Petitioners against the Respondent No.2 under Section 166 of Motor Vehicles Act is hereby Ananthramu vs Bharathi Axa Gen Ins Co Ltd on 2 May, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/150599696/

sentences.text: The Claim Petition filed by the Petitioners against the Respondent No.1 is hereby dismissed.

The Petitioner No.1 to 3 are entitled for total compensation of Rs.25,80,100/- along with cost and simple interest at the rate of 6% p.a., from the date of the Petition till the date of deposit of the Award amount.
The Respondent No.2 is liable to pay the compensation amount to the Petitioners.
The Respondent No.2 being the owner, is directed to deposit the Award amount and interest within 60 days from the date of the Award.

The compensation amount awarded to the Petitioner No.1 to 3 are apportioned SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 among them are as shown below:

Hence, the Tribunal was justified in holding that the Respondent No.2 permitted operating of the vehicle by an unauthorized person and the said act of Respondent No.2 amounts to fundamental SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 breach of policy condition within the meaning of Sec.149(2)(a)(ii) of the MV Act.
Therefore, the Tribunal was justified in exonerating the insurer on the ground that there is fundamental breach of policy condition.
In the instant case also, the Respondent No.2 being the owner cum rider of the offending motorcycle appeared before the Court through his Counsel, but, he did not choose to contest the matter by filing the Written Statement nor adduced any evidence claiming that he ridden the vehicle by possessing Driving license.

Under such circumstances, the insurance company cannot be fastened with liability of pay and recovery, when there is a clear breach of policy condition and the liability to pay compensation is on the owner of the vehicle.
The Sec.150(2) (a) (ii) of IMV Act speaks that no sum shall be payable by an insurer under sub Sec.(1) in respect of any Judgment or Award unless, before commencement of the proceedings in which the Judgment or Award is given the insurer had notice through the Court or, as the case may be, SCCH 15 MVC No.649/2023 the Claims Tribunal of the bringing of the proceedings, or in respect of such Judgment or Award so long as its execution is stayed pending in appeal, and an insurer to whom notice of the bringing of such any proceedings is so given shall be entitled to be made a party thereto, and to defend the action on any of the grounds, namely:-
